pros: Simple and intuitive resource distribution model
No parameters to tune or optimize
More aggressive penalty for high-degree nodes than Adamic-Adar
Strong theoretical foundation in resource allocation dynamics
Effective on networks with power-law degree distributions
cons: Cannot capture paths longer than 2 hops
Over-penalizes high-degree nodes in some network types
Less effective on dense graphs with many common neighbors
Does not consider edge weights or node attributes
Zero score for node pairs without common neighbors
Not suitable for bipartite networks without adaptation
Linear penalty may not reflect real-world resource dynamics
